# Data for the Chinese-language version of the figure "Beijing vs. its labs" (cn_figure_build.py in this folder reads this file).
# WRITTEN BY make_inputs.py from english_originals/figure_data.txt (the core's data) and zh_lines.txt: do not edit it here.
# Each block: the core's "@" line, Q, E, U lines and label place, unchanged; T, S and the label words in Simplified Chinese;
# Z = my Chinese for an English Q (shown as a translation, never inside quote marks). The core's own header follows.

# Data for the figure "Beijing vs. its labs" (scripts/cn_figure_build.py reads this file).
# One block per dated event:
#   @ LANE KIND DATE DATELABEL SAVED-ID
#   T  the line shown in the figure (my words)
#   S  the source as shown
#   Q  the page's own words (checked by the builder against the saved copy; spacing and quote style ignored)
#   E  my English rendering, where Q is Chinese
#   U  the address to link (only where the saved copy's own address is cut short or is a relay to avoid)
#   A  a second linked source, as SAVED-ID | source as shown
#   C  a short label drawn beside the mark on the strip: start|end dx dy words
#   N  the record's fixed number (core edit 7, Nov 25, 2026): a record added after the figure was made public takes the next
#      free number, so that no earlier record changes its number; records without N are numbered by date as before
# LANE: BH Beijing holds Nvidia back | BL Beijing is more open to Nvidia | CN companies reach for Nvidia | CH companies turn to home-made chips
# KIND: doc  a government document, an official on the record, or published state media (the legend's "on the record")
#       rec  a company, or a named person outside government, on the record (filing, results, a named executive or analyst)
#       press a press report citing unnamed people
# DATELABEL: "-" prints the date; otherwise the words given (use _ for a space).
# Lines starting "!" are extra quotations the builder must find (they back numbers in the panels): ! SAVED-ID | words
